sources.name: WHO 2008 Standard Acupuncture Point Locations (archive.org djvu text)

corrected_location: On the little-finger edge of the hand, in the soft dip at the wrist end of the hand bone leading to the little finger, where the palm skin meets the back-of-hand skin. Slide a finger up from the base of the little finger along that bone until you drop into the dip just before the wrist bone.
controversy: None on location; WHO 2008 and textbook sources agree.
notes: App says 'palm side', but the point sits on the ulnar border (red/white skin border), not on the palm face. 'Outer edge of the wrist below the base of the little finger' is otherwise right. Name Wangu = Wrist Bone is correct (Steve Woodley, TCM Wiki).

corrected_location: On the back of the hand, in the hollow where the thumb-side and index-side hand bones come together, a bit further back toward the wrist than the usual LI4 spot (not in the skin web itself).
controversy: Master Tung / Dong-family point (T 22.05), not in WHO 361 nor WHO extra-point nomenclature; both opened sources are Tung-specific, so effectively one school. Tung sources describe it as contraindicated in pregnancy.
notes: App text (web between thumb and index, nearer index) describes the LI4 area; Tung location is proximal to LI4 at the junction of the 1st and 2nd metacarpals. App pregnancyCaution=false conflicts with the Tung contraindication; recommend true or removing the point from a consumer app. Name 'Efficacious/Spirit Bone' acceptable (Spirit/Miraculous/Adroit Bone).

sources.name: PMC11410248 auricular lumbar sprain protocol (WFAS standard)
PMC8716479 History of Auriculotherapy (WHO 1990 ear-point nomenclature group)

corrected_location: On the ear, on the raised inner ridge (antihelix, not the outer rim), in its upper part just below where the ridge forks toward the top of the ear.
controversy: Lumbosacral vertebrae is a named WFAS/WHO-style ear point (AH9, on the antihelix body behind the abdomen point). Exact fraction ('a third down') not confirmed by any opened source; from memory the lumbosacral zone is the upper ~2/5 of the antihelix body, unverified. Ear charts (Nogier vs Chinese) differ.
notes: Two opened sources recognise the zone; neither gave the fraction. Risk: lay users may confuse 'upper ridge' with the outer helix rim; wording should say inner ridge.

sources.name: WHO 2008 Standard Acupuncture Point Locations (archive.org djvu text)

corrected_location: Two lines running up each side of the lower back: an inner line about one and a half thumb-widths from the spine and an outer line about three thumb-widths from the spine, in the waist area.
controversy: Zone label is not a single point; Bladder line 1 (BL23-25 etc.) and line 2 (BL52 etc.).
notes: WHO 2008: BL23 is 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior midline at L2; BL52 is 3 B-cun lateral at L2. App's 'one to two thumb-widths' only covers the inner line. Only WHO opened for this entry.

sources.name: WHO 2008 Standard Acupuncture Point Locations (archive.org djvu text)

corrected_location: On the buttock, in the fleshy area about a third of the way in from the side hip bump toward the tailbone dimple; roughly where a back pocket sits.
controversy: Not a defined point. Nearest standard point GB30 (Huantiao) lies at the junction of the outer one-third and inner two-thirds of the line from the greater trochanter to the sacral hiatus (WHO 2008); BL54 is 3 B-cun lateral at the 4th sacral foramen level.
notes: 'Back pocket' is a plausible lay landmark for the GB30/BL54 region but no source defines 'Hip Area' as such.

corrected_location: On the back of the hand, in the web between thumb and index finger, against the index-finger bone about halfway along it on the thumb side; it is the high spot of the muscle bulge when thumb and index are pressed together.
controversy: Several location methods are taught (muscle-bulge method vs. mid-second-metacarpal); they land close but not identical.
notes: App text is the common lay method and acceptable; add 'next to the index-finger bone'. Hegu = Joining Valley (alias 'Tiger's Mouth' also used). Pregnancy caution correct (TCM Wiki, Woodley).

corrected_location: At the base of the skull, in the hollows between the two big vertical neck muscles and the skull ridge, a few thumb-widths out to each side of the midline.
notes: App 'either side of the spine' is vague: GB20 is lateral, between the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius origins, at about GV16 level, not close to the midline. Fengchi = Wind Pool.

corrected_location: At the temple, in the tender hollow about a thumb-width behind the midpoint between the outer end of the eyebrow and the outer corner of the eye.
controversy: Recognised extra point EX-HN5 (WHO 1993 nomenclature; not in WHO 2008 361, which I confirmed lists no extra points). Widely recognised across texts (3+ sources found).
notes: App measures from the eyebrow end only and says 'beyond'; standard reference is the midpoint of brow-tail to outer canthus, then ~1 cun back. Close but imprecise. Press gently; avoid vigorous pressure near temporal artery.

corrected_location: On top of the foot, in the groove between the big toe and second toe bones, slide up from the web until the bones meet in a V; the point is in the hollow just before that V.
notes: App 'before the ankle' is vague and 'where the bones meet' could be read as the toe joints. Taichong = Supreme/Great Surge.

sources.name: WHO 2008 Standard Acupuncture Point Locations (archive.org djvu text)

notes: WHO fraction: junction of front third and back two-thirds of the heel-to-toe-web line (about one third from the toes). App wording 'a third of the way down from the base of toes' consistent. Code KI1 in WHO; app uses KD1. Yongquan = Gushing Spring.

sources.name: Master Tung site extra points list

corrected_location: On the back of the hand, in the groove between the long bones leading to the index and middle fingers, about half a thumb-width behind the knuckles.
controversy: Luozhen is an alias of Wailaogong (EX-UE8); some lists give Luozhen a separate code EX-UE14, so numbering is inconsistent. Not Tung-specific.
notes: App says 'between the knuckles' without 'behind'. 'Stiff Neck Point' is a fair gloss for Luozhen (fallen pillow).

sources.name: Master Tung site extra points list

corrected_location: On the back of the neck, about two thumb-widths above the prominent bump at the base of the neck (C7), then one thumb-width out to each side of the midline.
controversy: Code conflict: Jingbailao = EX-HN15 (WHO 1993), but sites list Bailao as EX-HN15 or EX-HN17.
notes: App text 'just above where the shoulder muscle meets the neck' places it too low/vague; standard is 2 cun above C7, 1 cun lateral. Recognised by at least 2 opened sources.
